full_judgment:
10. We have gone through the first information report of the case, charges framed against the accused person at the trial, the evidence of the prosecution witnesses as well as the impugned judgment. 

 11. We are now called upon to consider the legality and propriety of the impugned judgment in the light of the evidence on record. 

 12. Before coming to a discussion of the points raised on behalf of the appellant Motaleb, we would like to discuss the evidence on record. 

 41. Mr Khalilur Rahman, the learned Advocate on behalf of accused appellant, submitted that the allegations against the appellant have not been proved by sufficient evidence beyond reasonable doubt. Out of 18 witnesses none is an eye-witness of real occurrence of throwing acid. The motive of alleged offence was stated to be the bad proposals given by the accused Motaleb to the daughter of the informant for which his daughter revoked him which led Motaleb to throw acid and this has not been proved in any way. The deposition of the witnesses are contradictory and discrepant which are not legally admissible evidence; Most of the witnesses are co-related with each other and not virtually disinterested, as such, their deposition cannot be relied upon and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence are bad in law and wrong on facts which need to be set aside. 

 42. Mr Sk A Awal, the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the State, submitted that the impugned judgment of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Sirajgonj as being based on facts and evidence cannot be set aside. 

 43. On scrutiny of the evidence on record, it appears that the object of throwing acid was to give bad proposal to the daughter of informant PW 2 Monjuara and niece of the informant PW 9 Rekha but this fact has not been substantiated by evidence. PW 2 Monjuara did not utter a single word in this respect in her deposition and PW 9 made a contradictory statement in this regard. So, the basis of throwing acid by the accused Motaleb has not been proved. 

 47. Prosecution case is that Motaleb, Delwar Hossain, Gofur and others entered into the hut of the informant and Motaleb threw acid towards Shahida and Monjujra. PW 1 Sukchand in his examination in-chief stated in one place that Motaleb threw acid towards his wife and daughter, but in cross-examination, he stated that there was no light in the room and the room was dark and he cannot say who threw acid. PW 2 Monjuara and PW 3 Shahida expressed the same view in their respective deposition in this regard. PW 7 Mukdum Ali, PW 8 Rokeya Khatoon and PW 9 Rekha stated in their respective evidence that they heard from PWs 1 to 3 that Motaleb threw acid. When PW 1 to 3 denied that they did not see anybody to throw acid, then how PW 7 to 9 would hear from them and their assertion has not been substantiated. Moreover, PW 16 Md Masudal Hasan Chowdhury, who is the investigating officer of this case, testified that no witness mentioned any name to him about the throwing of acid. Thus throwing of acid by accused Motaleb towards the victims has not been proved. 

 49. It further appears from the evidence of the informant that Korban arranged to write ejhar by Advocate Abdul Hakim, the contents of the ejhar were not read out to him and he simply put his signature therein without going through the contents of it. It appears from the submissions of the learned Advocate for the defence that Korban in order to materialise his own wish, he directed the trend of the case in other direction and falsely involved the appellant Motaleb in this case. There seems to be substance in the submission of the learned Advocate and this fact at least, creates doubt about the prosecution case. 

 50. There is a glaring difference between the evidence of informant and the contents of ejahar. There are also so many contradictions and omissions in the evidence of PWs and under such circumstances, conviction of the appellant cannot be sustained. 

 51. It appears from evidence that there are no eye-witnesses in this case. The prosecution has to depend on circumstantial evidence alone. The law on circumstantial evidence is well settled by now. When there exists a well-knit and unbroken chain of circumstances leading to the unavoidable conclusion that none but the accused committed the alleged offence and no other hypothesis other than the guilt of the accused can be inferred from the given circumstances, a conviction can be safely based on circumstantial evidence alone. But the facts and circumstances of the present case fall far short of the standard requirement for safely basing an order of conviction on the untidy and almost stray evidence of PWs. 

 "In a criminal case, it is the duty of the court to review the entire evidence that has been produced by the prosecution and the defence. If after an examination of the whole evidence, the court is of the opinion that there is a reasonable possibility that the defence put forward by the accused might be true, it is clear that such a view reacts on the whole prosecution case. In these circumstances, the accused is entitled to benefit of doubt, not as a matter of grace but as of right, because the prosecution has not proved its case beyond reasonable doubt." 

 53. Thus, it is very clear that the offence under section 326A is quite specific and distinctive having specific ingredients keeping in view the above distinguishing features and ingredients of the offence under section 326A. If we examine in the light of the evidence on record and the facts of the case, the propriety and legality of the impugned judgment and order passed against the appellant Motaleb cannot be sustained and we cannot but hold that the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence under section 326A of the Penal Code are wholly bad, illegal and unwarranted by law and facts and the same must be set aside. There is not an iota of reliable evidence on record to establish such ingredients of the offence under section 326A of the Penal Code and to punish the accused appellant Motaleb. When main charge against the accused appellant Motaleb under section 326A of the Penal Code has not been proved then the charge against the appellant under sections 457 and 307 of the Penal Code has automatically gone which cannot be sustained. Moreover, it appears from facts, circumstances and evidence on record that the charge against the accused Motaleb under sections 457/307 of the Penal Code has not been proved and he is entitled to be acquitted from the charge under sections 457 and 307 of the Penal Code. The evidence adduced by the prosecution in the case can at best provide suspicion, against the accused but suspicion however high and probable, can never take the place of legal evidence. 

 54. We have given our anxious consideration to the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence on record but we fail to persuade ourselves to subscribe to the view taken by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. We are therefore, constrained to hold that the prosecution failed to prove its case against the accused appellant beyond reasonable doubt and he is entitled to acquittal accordingly. The appeal succeeds.
